description: The compass view-model (Features WV1, P2.core; catalog ui-compass): a heading in degrees clockwise from north with its 8-point name, and a bearing for every marker on the strip. Core space (CORE_CONVENTION): ground axes x and z, yaw in radians about +Y, positive turning +Z toward +X; a yaw of t faces (sin t, cos t). North is an input to op view (northYaw, the core-space yaw that faces north) and a world fact to ops north and world_view (P2.core-north): a geography's georeference states it (northYaw = georeference.rotationRad, 0 when absent), and a world that states none gets the declared default (contract defaultNorthYaw, core +Z, east at +X). Runner: src/ui/hud-corpus.ts. Op view runs compassView({yaw, northYaw, position, markers, span?, mirrored?}) -> {ok:true, value} or {ok:false, refusal:{code, field}}; op heading runs compassHeading(yaw, northYaw); op cardinal runs compassCardinal(degrees); op north runs worldNorth(geography?) -> {ok:true, value:{northYaw, source}} or a refusal; op world_view runs worldCompassView({geography?, yaw? | facing?, position, markers, span?, mirrored?}) -> {ok:true, north, value} or a refusal. One exception to the null rule below: span: null means the span is not stated (the default span, contract spanNull), never a non-finite span, in ops view and world_view alike (P2.core's m3, settled in P1.core-slots). A level that lays the IR's plan out mirrored (Unreal's village: X = x, Y = z) keeps the IR's numbers for positions, hands its facing as the ground direction facing {x, z} in them, never its own yaw, and says mirrored: true, so the strip puts each marker on the side the player sees it (contract mirroredLevel, relativeRule). Every case is {name, op, input, expected}; numbers compare within tolerance, everything else exactly, object key sets included (a key TypeScript leaves undefined is absent). A non-finite number is written as null in an input. Regenerate with npm run hud-corpora; npm run hud-corpora:check fails on any difference.
sources: New in core. The 8 points and their rounding (a half-way heading rounds clockwise) match Godot compass_panel.gd cardinal_of, Unreal SInsimulVillageHud and Babylon genre-hud-model compassPoint; the heading as facing less north matches Unreal SInsimulVillageHud::SetCompass; the default span is Godot's SPAN.

Inputs are synthetic. No case sits on an exact visibility edge, where a last-bit difference between engines would flip it, nor on the heading's 0/360 wrap (a facing along an axis is written with an exact 0).

North (P2.core-north, UU gaps 4.9): GeoreferenceIR.rotationRad (NF.C6) where the world states one; else core +Z, the reading core's backdrop already gives a plan (editor/layout/backdrop.ts: N is +z, E is +x). The mirrored level is Unreal's village (InsimulVillageDirector NorthYaw 90: "The IR's +z is north; that is Unreal's +Y"; SInsimulVillageHud::SetCompass bearing = yaw - NorthYaw, which a mirror makes run backwards; its yaw grows clockwise seen from above, SInsimulVillageHud.cpp:246, so facing (X, Y) the player's right is (-Y, X)). A reflection is undone by no rotation, so the mirrored strip keeps the world's labels and draws relative in the player's own sense (mirrored: true; P2.core-north round 2, the critic's B1).

contract.spanNull: span: null is not stated: the default span (defaultSpanDegrees), never not_finite
contract.relativeRange: (-180, 180], positive to the right as the player sees it
contract.relativeRule: stripRelative(bearing, heading, mirrored): unmirrored relative = wrap(bearing - heading); mirrored: true, relative = wrap(heading - bearing) (labels run N W S E clockwise); wrap into (-180, 180]. Cardinal ticks use the same rule
contract.northRule: a georeference states north: northYaw = rotationRad (0 when absent; not wrapped); no geography or no georeference: defaultNorthYaw
worldRefusalOrder: facing given twice or not at all
contract.mirroredLevel: level X = IR x, level Y = IR z; positions are the IR's numbers as they stand; facing = {x: Forward.X, z: Forward.Y}, i.e. an Unreal yaw d faces {x: cos d, z: sin d}; and mirrored: true. Heading, cardinal and bearings stay the world's labels; relative and offset are in the player's own sense (a marker on the player's right in the level is on the strip's right) and the view carries mirrored: true. The minimap passes mirrored too (contract projectionMirrored)
